_about: Scientific points of interest in Jezero Crater used by MARSCOPE. Positions are APPROXIMATE (typically within ~0.5-1 km), compiled from public Mars 2020 mission maps and checked by eye against the bundled CTX orthoimage; verify against official JPL traverse maps before any operational use. 'observations' are reported measurements with their sources; 'interpretations' are scientific interpretations from the cited literature; 'priority' is a MARSCOPE planning weight (expert judgement, 0-1), NOT a NASA ranking. Entries with origin 'marscope_derived' were identified by MARSCOPE from the CTX DTM and have no published name.

references.Fassett2005: Fassett, C. I. & Head, J. W. (2005). Fluvial sedimentary deposits on Mars: Ancient deltas in a crater lake in the Nili Fossae region. Geophysical Research Letters 32, L14201.
references.Ehlmann2008: Ehlmann, B. L. et al. (2008). Clay minerals in delta deposits and organic preservation potential on Mars. Nature Geoscience 1, 355-358.
references.Goudge2015: Goudge, T. A. et al. (2015). Assessing the mineralogy of the watershed and fan deposits of the Jezero crater paleolake system, Mars. JGR Planets 120, 775-808.
references.Horgan2020: Horgan, B. H. N. et al. (2020). The mineral diversity of Jezero crater: Evidence for possible lacustrine carbonates on Mars. Icarus 339, 113526.
references.Stack2020: Stack, K. M. et al. (2020). Photogeologic map of the Perseverance rover field site in Jezero crater constructed by the Mars 2020 Science Team. Space Science Reviews 216, 127.
references.Mangold2021: Mangold, N. et al. (2021). Perseverance rover reveals an ancient delta-lake system and flood deposits at Jezero crater, Mars. Science 374, 711-717.
references.Farley2022: Farley, K. A. et al. (2022). Aqueously altered igneous rocks sampled on the floor of Jezero crater, Mars. Science 377, eabo2196.
references.Liu2022: Liu, Y. et al. (2022). An olivine cumulate outcrop on the floor of Jezero crater, Mars. Science 377, 1513-1519.
references.Hurowitz2025: Hurowitz, J. A. et al. (2025). Redox-driven mineral and organic associations in Jezero Crater, Mars. Nature.
references.NASA_M2020: NASA/JPL-Caltech Mars 2020 Perseverance mission pages and press releases (science.nasa.gov/mission/mars-2020-perseverance).
references.NASA_Depot: NASA/JPL-Caltech (Dec 2022 - Jan 2023). Perseverance deposits samples at the Three Forks sample depot.

pois.name: Octavia E. Butler Landing (Perseverance landing site)
minerals_reported: Igneous (basaltic) floor rocks with aqueous alteration products (Máaz formation)
pois.water_evidence: Floor rocks show alteration minerals indicating interaction with water after emplacement (Farley2022).

observations.text: Floor rocks sampled nearby are igneous and contain secondary minerals formed by aqueous alteration.

interpretations.text: The crater floor here belongs to igneous units (Máaz) emplaced on the floor and later altered by water.

pois.name: Séítah (olivine-rich floor unit)
pois.water_evidence: Olivine-rich rocks partly altered to carbonate and other secondary phases record later water-rock interaction (Liu2022).

observations.text: Rover instruments characterised an olivine-rich cumulate outcrop.
Séítah is mapped as a distinct unit on the crater floor, including aeolian bedforms.

interpretations.text: Séítah formed by settling of olivine crystals in a thick magma body or lava lake, later altered by water.

objectives: Note: sand ripples are a mobility hazard

pois.name: Kodiak butte
pois.water_evidence: Inclined layers seen from the rover are interpreted as delta foresets, recording deposition into a standing lake (Mangold2021).

observations.text: Long-range rover images show stratified layers with inclined geometry.

interpretations.text: Kodiak is an erosional remnant of the western delta; its stratigraphy records lake-level changes.

pois.name: Three Forks sample depot
pois.water_evidence: Depot holds duplicate samples including delta-front sedimentary rocks (NASA_Depot).

observations.text: Perseverance placed ten sealed sample tubes on the surface here between Dec 2022 and Jan 2023 as a backup cache for Mars Sample Return.

pois.name: Delta front (Hawksbill Gap area)
pois.water_evidence: Fan-shaped sedimentary deposit at the mouth of an inlet valley, with layered fine-grained rocks deposited in a lake (Fassett2005; Mangold2021).

observations.text: CRISM orbital spectra show Fe/Mg smectite and carbonate signatures in the fan deposits.
Orbital mineralogy of the fan resembles the watershed, consistent with transported sediment.
Rover images show layered sedimentary rocks at the delta front.

interpretations.text: The western fan is a delta built into an ancient lake; its fine-grained layers are prime targets for preserved organics and biosignatures.

objectives: Characterise lake sediments and their mineralogy

pois.name: Delta top near Belva crater
minerals_reported: Fe/Mg smectite and carbonate (orbital, CRISM, fan deposits)
pois.water_evidence: Upper fan surfaces preserve channel deposits and coarse fluvial sediments transported by rivers into the lake (Mangold2021).

observations.text: Belva is an impact crater (~0.9 km) on the fan whose walls expose fan stratigraphy; Perseverance imaged it in 2023.
Fan deposits show smectite and carbonate signatures from orbit.

interpretations.text: Boulder-rich upper-fan layers may record high-energy floods late in the lake's history.

objectives: Read fan stratigraphy in Belva's walls
Sample river-transported clasts from the watershed

pois.name: Belva crater (rim)
pois.water_evidence: Natural cross-section through the delta deposits.

observations.text: Crater walls expose layered fan deposits imaged by Perseverance.

objectives: Hazard: steep inner walls - observe from rim

pois.name: Bright Angel / Cheyava Falls (Neretva Vallis)
minerals_reported: Fe-phosphate and Fe-sulfide associated with organic carbon in 'leopard spot' features (rover)
pois.water_evidence: Mudstone in the Neretva Vallis channel deposited by water, with reaction fronts formed during later fluid interaction (Hurowitz2025).

observations.text: The Cheyava Falls rock (sample 'Sapphire Canyon') shows millimetre-scale reaction fronts ('leopard spots') with Fe-phosphate and Fe-sulfide minerals and organic-carbon signals.

interpretations.text: The features are a POTENTIAL biosignature: they could be produced by microbial redox reactions, but abiotic explanations have not been ruled out.

objectives: Compare with laboratory analysis of returned samples

pois.name: Neretva Vallis inlet
minerals_reported: Watershed clays and olivine-carbonate transported into the fan (orbital)
pois.water_evidence: A river valley that breached the western crater rim and fed the delta (Fassett2005).

observations.text: Valley network enters Jezero through the western rim; visible in CTX and THEMIS images.

interpretations.text: Jezero was an open-basin lake fed by inlet valleys and drained by an outlet.

objectives: Channel-floor deposits and lake inflow history

pois.name: Inner-rim margin unit (carbonate-bearing)
pois.water_evidence: Carbonate concentrated along the inner crater margin has been proposed to be lacustrine (shoreline) carbonate (Horgan2020).

observations.text: Orbital spectra show strong carbonate signatures in a band along the inner western margin.

interpretations.text: Possibly carbonates precipitated near the lake shore, which on Earth can preserve biosignatures; alternative origins (e.g. altered olivine-rich deposits) remain possible.

objectives: Test lacustrine vs non-lacustrine carbonate origin

pois.name: Western crater rim (Witch Hazel Hill area)
pois.water_evidence: Not primarily a water target; rim rocks predate the lake.

observations.text: Perseverance climbed the crater rim and began exploring this area in late 2024.

interpretations.text: Rim rocks are expected to include ancient crust uplifted or excavated by the Jezero impact, older than the lake deposits.

pois.name: Unnamed ~1.3 km crater on northern floor
pois.water_evidence: Unknown - no published analysis used by MARSCOPE.

observations.text: Circular depression with raised rim identified by MARSCOPE in the CTX DTM and orthoimage.

interpretations.text: A natural excavation that could expose subsurface floor material (MARSCOPE hypothesis, unverified).

objectives: Remote characterisation of subsurface floor units

pois.name: Unnamed ~1.5 km crater on eastern floor
pois.water_evidence: Unknown - no published analysis used by MARSCOPE.

observations.text: Fresh-looking bowl-shaped crater identified by MARSCOPE in the CTX DTM and THEMIS night IR (warm ejecta).

interpretations.text: Warm nighttime ejecta suggests blocky, rock-rich material (MARSCOPE interpretation of THEMIS brightness).

objectives: Sample excavated floor material at the ejecta blanket
